posts.title: Flirt, a Patch Series Code Review Tool, Goes Open Source - Re-review After Force-Pushes and Its Current Maturity
posts.description: Flirt, a code review tool for the patch series workflow, was open-sourced on Codeberg on 2026-10-05. The author says it is not yet ready for general use.

posts.title: One Developer Goes Back from Deno to Node.js — Reading Type Stripping and the pnpm Release Delay Next to the Official Docs
posts.description: A retrospective on returning from Deno to Node.js, set beside the official docs: fnm, pnpm minimumReleaseAge and trustPolicy, and Node type stripping.

posts.description: How the experimental iroh content discovery pairs the BitTorrent Mainline DHT with a small UDP address index, and the limits its authors list.

posts.title: Disclosure With a Price Tag — The $2.3 Million Estimate a Texas City Issued for a Flock Records Request
posts.description: The Texas Tribune reports North Richland Hills quoted $2.3 million for Flock records. The invoice formula, the city’s reply, and the state complaint process.

posts.title: Style Mimicry and Signature Reproduction Are Different Problems — The Report That ChatGPT Cartoons Carry Real Cartoonists’ Signatures
posts.description: Nieman Lab reports ChatGPT signs New Yorker-style cartoons with real cartoonists’ names. What the reporter documented and what OpenAI and the magazine said.

posts.title: JetBrains' Czech Entity and Its 2025 Net Loss — Reading the Unconsolidated Filing Line by Line

posts.title: How to Read the Factor Overview: Stack Effects, Quotations and Combinators in a Language Where Values Flow on a Stack
posts.description: A map for first-time readers of Factor, the stack-based concatenative language: stack effects, quotations, combinators, the only-f-is-false rule and tuples.

posts.description: James Ross calls his title a bit hyperbolic and writes that open source as he has known it is dying. His argument and cited cases, checked against sources.
